prompt.brief: Design a research-to-execution platform for reinforcement-learning trading agents that uses realistic backtests, strict risk controls, paper trading, and low-latency order execution.
successSignals: Define immutable market-data versions, point-in-time features, action/reward contracts, experiment lineage, and reproducible agent artifacts.
Model fees, slippage, latency, liquidity, partial fills, limits, market regimes, and leakage-resistant train/validation/test splits.
Separate offline training and simulation from a guarded paper/live execution path with idempotent orders and kill switches.
Explain risk limits, policy approval, drift, rollback, broker failure, auditability, observability, and safe degradation.

functional: Ingest and validate market data, build point-in-time datasets, train agents, run reproducible backtests, and compare risk-adjusted results.
Support paper trading and approved live execution with portfolio state, pre-trade risk checks, order status reconciliation, and kill switches.
Version policies and data, audit every decision/order, detect regime changes, and recover safely from broker or market-data outages.
nonFunctional: Keep execution decisions within the configured trading latency budget and require statistically robust, leakage-free evaluation before promotion.
Scale parallel training and backtests across many instruments without unbounded synchronous work or unsafe live rollout.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Years of tick or bar data across thousands of instruments
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

architecture.title: Reinforcement Learning Trading System domain architecture
architecture.summary: Design a research-to-execution platform for reinforcement-learning trading agents that uses realistic backtests, strict risk controls, paper trading, and low-latency order execution. The design makes reinforcement learning trading system decisions durable, isolates slow or external work behind replayable boundaries, and exposes freshness, authorization, and recovery state to operators and clients.

layers.label: Market evidence and policy

layers.description: Feed quality, exposure, latency, reconciliation, and kill-switch signals protect capital.

deepDives.title: No future data and reproducibility
points: Pin market sequence, feature window, strategy artifact, and policy for each decision.
Separate simulation clocks and datasets from live order routing.
Record the exact evidence and model version behind every order intent.

deepDives.title: Unknown execution outcomes
points: Use venue client order IDs and query-after-timeout before retrying a reinforcement learning trading system order.
Treat partial fills, rejects, cancels, and out-of-order events as explicit state transitions.
Reconcile positions from fills and account statements rather than trusting one callback.

deepDives.title: Risk and kill switches
points: Evaluate account, instrument, and global limits on the hot path with bounded latency.
Make kill switches versioned, scoped, expiring, and independently observable.
Alert on feed gaps, stale features, order latency, exposure, PnL, and reconciliation drift.

tradeoffs.title: Model sophistication versus control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep a simple auditable baseline and add complex policy only behind simulation, canary, and kill-switch controls.
tradeoffs.caution: A more accurate model is not safe if its input, rollout, or failure behavior is opaque.

tradeoffs.title: Low latency versus durable audit
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use an in-memory hot path backed by an append-only decision and execution log.
tradeoffs.caution: Dropping audit events to shave latency makes incident reconstruction and reconciliation impossible.

tradeoffs.title: Single venue versus routing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with one venue adapter and add routing once failure and reconciliation semantics are proven.
tradeoffs.caution: Multi-venue routing multiplies duplicate, partial-fill, and fee edge cases.

commonMistakes: Training or simulating on future information.
Retrying an unknown venue result as if the order definitely failed.
Letting a model bypass deterministic risk limits.
Updating positions from requests instead of execution evidence.
Building a kill switch that is not scoped, expiring, tested, or observable.

followUps.question: How do you avoid duplicate live orders?
followUps.answer: Use a durable client order ID, conditional order state, venue idempotency, and query-after-timeout reconciliation.

followUps.question: How do you handle a market-data gap?
followUps.answer: Mark features stale, halt or degrade the affected strategy, and require a fresh sequence before resuming.

followUps.question: How do you isolate research from production?
followUps.answer: Use separate credentials, queues, storage, and execution adapters; only signed, approved artifacts can cross into live routing.

rubric.description: The answer addresses the reinforcement learning trading system workflow, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure contract.
The answer identifies the authoritative reinforcement learning trading system state, versioning or deduplication boundary, and how derived views converge.
The answer partitions reinforcement learning trading system traffic, isolates hot keys, and moves fan-out, retries, or rebuilds behind bounded asynchronous work.
The answer names freshness, backlog, error, cost, and recovery signals tied to the reinforcement learning trading system user experience.
